source.title: Resolved wet particle-size cumulative distributions and reported moments for Schmieder 2023
source.citation: Schmieder B.K.L., Pannusch V.B., Vannieuwenhuyse L., Briesen H., Minceva M. (2023). Influence of Flow Rate, Particle Size, and Temperature on Espresso Extraction Kinetics. Foods 12(15):2871. Figure A1(b) and section 2.4. Digitisation and unresolved-head reconstruction by Puckworks; these are not the authors' raw instrument files.
source.obtained: python/puckworks_tools/sources/schmieder2023_psd.py renders page 15 of the published PDF (SHA-256 e7ff3e581fb3c5fc3e0148124929748aa153ab0990d8372079c02bd33a0e2a75) at 600 dpi, cropping x=2540,y=4020,width=1710,height=1260. Cumulative Q3, not the plotted density q3, supplies the volume measure. Full coloured errorbar spans give central values, including gaps occluded by another colour. Diameter uses 315 pixels per log10 decade; the mapping differs from the labelled intermediate ticks by at most 1 pixel. Q3 uses y=1099 for 0 and y=130 for 100 percent. Sub-3.04 um points are unresolved and omitted. Three columns where q3 and Q3 cross (x=1044,1067,1092) are omitted. A least-squares monotonic projection removes small digitisation reversals; the largest change is 0.002580 volume fraction (GL1.4), and all raw readings are retained. The endpoint (1000 um,1) is an explicit support assumption. Reported D32, D43 and their SDs are transcribed from section 2.4.
source.uncertainty: Resolved, separated pixel centres can be read to approximately 2-3 pixels (0.21-0.31 percentage points of volume); occlusion and the 0.258 percentage-point monotonicity correction motivate a conservative 1 percentage-point reading sensitivity. This is an estimated digitisation allowance, not a statistical confidence interval. Measurement error bars in the figure are not transcribed as independent errors. The omitted fine head, interpolation over omitted crossings, within-bin shape, and assumed terminal support add uncertainty. Reported D32 SDs are 1.6,3.2,1.4 um and D43 SDs are 7.6,17,18 um for GL1.4,1.7,2.0. A distribution's D32 is nonlinear: imposing the reported mean D32 on the digitised mean curve is a reconstruction convention, not recovery of every replicate.

source.notes: This dataset is an exploratory case input, not an added espresso-response fitting target. The default calibration keeps its historical reconstructed PSD. The explicit wet_cdf case uses uniform volume density in diameter between resolved coordinates. The first cumulative share is represented by one unresolved-head diameter chosen to match the published D32 (or a declared SD sensitivity); head mass and diameter must be admissible. D43 remains an unfitted cross-check. The wet measurement uses HELOS/BR and Quixel; Fig.A1(a) uses dry Rodos dispersion. These wet equivalent-sphere diameters do not measure dry puck geometry, intact-cell diffusion distances, or a moisture/gas-relaxation radius.

source_basis: The wet input uses the resolved cumulative volume distribution Q3 from Schmieder et al. (2023), Fig. A1(b), and the wet D32/D43 means and SDs in section 2.4. It is a digitisation of the published figure, not the authors' raw instrument data. Each resolved interval has uniform volume density in diameter; midpoint quadrature preserves its volume and D43 and approximates D32 within 1e-7.

The unresolved fraction below the first resolved coordinate is placed at one effective diameter to impose the reported D32. This head diameter is derived, not a measured fine-particle shape. D32 agreement is a constraint, while D43 is an unfitted cross-check. Applying a mean D32 to a mean CDF does not recover the replicate distributions.

The sub-3.04 µm head and three density/CDF crossings are omitted from the digitisation. Interpolation over those crossings, within-bin shape, an assumed terminal support at 1000 µm, occlusion and the monotonic projection remain uncertain. Raw readings and the projection are retained in the dataset. These runs do not sample all those uncertainties.

The ±1 SD variants move the reported D32 target and only the derived head diameter; the resolved CDF and head fraction stay fixed. They are fixed input sensitivities, not a confidence band or independent replicate predictions.

All shared and nuisance values remain at the preserved v2 calibration, including each grinding level's bare permeability κ₀. There is no refit or rescaling of κ₀ for the new particle input. Registry values for unfitted parameters and the existing V1 conditions also remain fixed.

The builder's pore-air relaxation time follows wet D32 through its moisture-diffusion closure; this use of a wet equivalent-sphere diameter is not independently validated as a gas-relaxation radius or intact-cell diffusion distance. One variant copies the original case's air τ per experiment to expose this coupling. The builder also changes preparation heterogeneity σ through the volume share below 100 µm. Holding only air τ fixed therefore still mixes particle transport with the changed permeability spread. Wet and dry particle geometry need not coincide.

The 32-class numerical check replaces only bed.size_classes in the nominal wet16 final spec. All non-class fields, including air τ and preparation heterogeneity, remain exactly fixed. Its case metadata comes from the normally built 32-class recipe, but that recipe alone would also change the builder's class-interpolated fines share and derived heterogeneity.

Scores use the existing V1 absolute relative-error rule ≤10%, with the authors' Eq. 3 cup masses. Every scenario retains denominators of 60 λ values and 180 cup masses; failed, incomplete, missing and nonfinite predictions cannot count as successes. First drops and shot times use the solver's summary convention, and their ranges include completed shots only.

This is a conditional input audit on the V1 calibration data, not independent validation. It selects no best variant, promotes no input automatically, and changes no calibration defaults or scientific acceptance gates.

fixed.reason: M1.1 fills the complete intraparticle pore-water inventory behind the front (fraction 1), rather than counting only the mobile share. This is a water-volume accounting choice, not a fit to shot times. The effective-loading approximation is documented in the startup model and remains subject to validation against independent uptake measurements.

The initial effective connectivity deficit is a grade D model assumption (0.5), separate from coffee CO2; it is not a measured gas volume fraction. None of the calibration observables identifies a transient relative-permeability law. It is held at its prior rather than fitted to the held-out V4 first-drop delay or flow rise.
The effective connectivity-to-relative-permeability exponent is a grade D closure (3), not measured for these pucks. Held fixed; the V4 transient, V3 and V5 shot times do not select it.

The pore-air relaxation time uses (D32/2)^2/(pi^2 D), capped at 600 s, with D = 2.5e-11 m^2/s from the independent Mateus moisture-uptake range. Using moisture diffusion for air clearance is a grade D model assumption. Neither this diffusivity nor its time scale is fitted to held-out shots.
In M1.1 this is the fixed effective-loading normalization inherited from the extraction model, distinct from the full intraparticle water inventory. It is not fitted to startup observations.

Species kernel diffusivities trade off with the coffee's contents (correlation −0.89 to −0.95): their posterior SD was 2–12× the prior's, and free fits drifted 2–5× outside the literature priors (caffeine to 8×10⁻¹¹, trigonelline to the 1×10⁻⁹ bound). The species surface-pool scales carry the species' λ instead.
Not identified by V1 (see the caffeine diffusivity).
Not identified by V1 (see the caffeine diffusivity).
Weakly identified by V1 (posterior SD 1.15× the prior's; it trades off with the extractable fraction); fixing it did not raise the cost.
Not identified by V1 (posterior SD 44× the prior's once the lumped diffusivity is fixed); the surface flux is fast at any value in its range, so only the surface pool's size matters.
Not identified by V1 (posterior SD 1.6× the prior's when added at the V1 optimum); the residuals lean towards less swelling (Wald z 2.4 towards 0).
Weakly identified by V1 (posterior SD 0.4–0.7× the prior's) with no evidence against the registry value (Wald z 0.8); the CO₂ model is being re-anchored in the input models.

θ is fixed at its mechanistic default, 0 (the insoluble cell walls hold the particle envelope), not chosen by fit quality: it is collinear with the bed permeability, whose fitted values move to absorb it. `calibrate --sensitivity` reports the θ = 0.27 case as a structural sensitivity.

scenarios.spec_construction: Build a wet 32-class case for its PSD/classes and metadata, then replace only bed.size_classes in the corresponding wet16 final spec; all other fields are copied from wet16, including pore-air tau and preparation heterogeneity. The simulated spec therefore differs from rebuilding the 32-class recipe alone.
